model.name: H.R. 997 (119th)
model.title: National Taxpayer Advocate Enhancement Act of 2025

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Public Law):

blocks.text: National Taxpayer Advocate Enhancement Act of 2025

This act authorizes the National Taxpayer Advocate to appoint legal counsel within the Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS) to report directly to the National Taxpayer Advocate. The act also expands the authority of the National Taxpayer Advocate to take personnel actions with respect to local taxpayer advocates (located in each state) to include actions with respect to any employee of TAS.

Prior to this act, pursuant to a Department of the Treasury order, all legal counsel whose duties include providing legal advice to any official in any office or bureau of Treasury were part of the Legal Division within Treasury and under the supervision of the General Counsel, with limited exceptions. TAS assists taxpayers in matters involving the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and is part of the IRS, within Treasury.

The National Taxpayer Advocate Enhancement Act of 2025 lets the National Taxpayer Advocate hire its own legal counsel inside the Taxpayer Advocate Service (TAS), and that lawyer would report directly to the National Taxpayer Advocate. The act also gives the National Taxpayer Advocate more power over personnel decisions. Before, that power covered only the local taxpayer advocates, who work in each state. Now it extends to any employee of TAS.

The change matters because of how legal staff were organized before. Under a Treasury Department order, lawyers who give legal advice to officials in Treasury offices and bureaus were generally part of a Legal Division under the General Counsel, with only limited exceptions. TAS helps taxpayers with problems involving the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and it is itself part of the IRS, which sits within Treasury.
